correctness.rationale: For every a>0, 0<=b<omega, the exact polar calculation yields P=r^4(1-(b/omega)sin4theta), bounded between (1-b/omega)r^4 and (1+b/omega)r^4, and Pdot=-4a r^2 P. This ensures global asymptotic stability. For b<=a, r^2+P is proper C-infinity strict and has Hessian 2I. For b>a, any C2 Morse candidate has leading Hessian H>0, while averaging its forced nonpositive leading Lie derivative over the four rotations gives (tr H/2)(b-a)<=0, impossible. The same exact group average rules out a strict quadratic for b=a; odd degree polynomials cannot be globally positive definite. Standalone symbolic replay verified the general Lie identity, symmetry, and radial formula; 600 rational tests are supplementary, not proof.

The closest public mathematical-record claim concerns flat time changes, not this polynomial family. value.rationale: Fourfold covariance uniquely selects the two canonical cubic monomials; this is not an arbitrary coefficient slice. The result identifies the exact point at which a globally stable, polynomially certified flow loses every positive-Hessian Lyapunov certificate without a dynamical stability bifurcation. A sharp minimum global strict polynomial degree (2 versus 4) and explicit quartic witness distinguish Morse and polynomial certification, directly addressing the recently motivated semisimple-center gap.
